name: matmul_shared_row_buffer
task: This project computes the Gram matrix G = A * A^T of a synthetic integer matrix, split across multiple translation units: include/matrix.h + src/matrix.cpp (a row-major 64-bit integer matrix and a deterministic random-matrix generator), include/matmul.h + src/matmul.cpp (serial and OpenMP-parallel matrix multiplication plus a parallel transpose), include/pipeline.h + src/pipeline.cpp (compute_gram_matrix(), built on transpose_parallel() and multiply_parallel(), and a trace helper), and src/main.cpp (the profiling entry point). multiply_parallel() in src/matmul.cpp parallelizes the outer loop over rows of A with '#pragma omp parallel for', but each iteration first stages row i of A into a std::vector 'row_buffer' that is declared outside the parallel loop and therefore shared by all threads. Threads overwrite each other's staged row while still multiplying, so the products mix entries from different rows of A and the parallel result differs from multiply_serial(); compute_gram_matrix() in src/pipeline.cpp inherits the error because it calls multiply_parallel(). Fix multiply_parallel() so the result is identical to multiply_serial() on every input shape while the row loop stays parallelized with OpenMP (do not simply remove the pragma or serialize the loop; for example make the staging buffer private to each thread, or read directly from A). Do not change any function signature declared in include/matrix.h, include/matmul.h or include/pipeline.h.
notes: build_command compiles the profiling entry point at build/app (src/main.cpp -> matrix.cpp, matmul.cpp, pipeline.cpp). This binary must be built and then executed via run_command to drive DiscoPoP's instrumentation and produce its dynamic profiling output, including dynamic_dependencies, over the parallel row loop in multiply_parallel(). test_command builds and runs a separate correctness harness at build/run_tests (from tests/test_main.cpp); it is independent of the profiling binary and should not be used as the DiscoPoP execution target. Both binaries link the same matrix.cpp, matmul.cpp, pipeline.cpp object files, so no separate CMake/Meson/etc. configuration is required — plain 'make' is sufficient to build, run, and test.
